items.title: Dan Barrett interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: There’s Vic Dickinson and going back further, J.C. Higginbotham. ... My dad had some 78s around the house ... one of them featured J.C. Higginbotham on trombone.

ctx.x: Talk to us about playing the trombone, and how you try to impose your will over perhaps an imprecise instrument.

Well, remember I always wanted to play the trumpet and in recent years I’m starting to play more and more cornet actually. But I try to approach the trumpet, or I try to approach the trombone more like a trumpet. And Louis is my big hero actually. If I had to pick one it would be Louis. And then I don’t know who the second one would be you © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

know, I mean there are so many guys I love, but Louis is number one. And I keep thinking about him and I keep thinking about playing as simply as I can. And this may be something that comes with age. I remember when I was 15 trying to do everything under the sun. And I was about 18 when I heard my first Charlie Parker record and — well no I can’t say that, I guess I was in high school — and I just didn’t get it. I really didn’t get it.
